companion_apps.name: Brother My Stitch Monitor
companion_apps.notes: Android 2.1.5 (34) and the earliest preserved 1.0.0 release were reviewed statically. Their discovery and monitoring behavior is reported here without copying the vendor client's unsafe TLS policy.

identity.notes: machine-id comes from /info and MAC from SNMP when available. The IP address is a locator, not identity. The SNMP sysName/model field may be displayed as a fallback but is not used to select an EV1 or any other variant by numeric ID.

methods.notes: Use SNMPv1 GET on UDP 161 with community public and a fresh request ID for every newly encoded datagram. Probe the directed subnet broadcast first, then make one limited-broadcast attempt to 255.255.255.255 if no valid responder is found. Do not start with a network-wide unicast sweep. Require the exact, case-sensitive host- resources description brother sewing, then complete the HTTPS /info capability check before presenting this family. sysName or a numeric model ID is never a stand-alone matcher.

tls.notes: Require an explicit user decision before the first HTTPS /info request. Display the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint and the already matched machine address, and hold an approved pin only in memory against the discovered address/MAC. Fetch /info with that volatile pin, require a nonempty machine-id and monitoring capability, then atomically persist the pin to machine-id before any other monitoring endpoint. Subsequent connections require the pinned identity. Never accept every certificate or every hostname as the vendor client does. The actual certificate chain and renewal behavior have not been captured.

device.name: Brother My Stitch Monitor Embroidery Machines
device.notes:
READ-ONLY MONITORING ONLY. This spec never starts, stops or moves the machine, transfers a design, uploads an image, registers push notifications, invokes a lens function or updates firmware. Only the four HTTPS GETs below are executable. A feature's presence in the shared vendor library is not evidence that a machine or this spec supports it.
The Skitch PP1 is a different, BLE-only product covered by brother-skitch-pp1.yaml and is deliberately not extended by this file. ScanNCut is also outside this spec: a document format without a recovered local transport is not a Brother monitoring protocol.

openness.notes: Brother documents app/model compatibility and wireless setup but does not publish a third-party monitoring API. SNMP, HTTPS and JSON details are implementation-derived and remain unconfirmed against hardware.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: There is no physical pairing button or vendor pairing window for this API. SNMP identification and the user's certificate-pin approval are the authorization flow; access to the same LAN is the network gate.

exclusivity.notes: Concurrent client limits have not been measured. Bonding here means the client stores its user-approved certificate pin, not a Bluetooth bond or a limit established on the machine.
exclusivity.recovery: Close other monitoring clients if the machine stops responding, and check that the address and certificate pin still belong to the intended machine. Do not delete Wi-Fi settings or perform a full-data reset just because a client is connected elsewhere.

pairing.notes: The vendor app's local API does not negotiate an account credential. Nevertheless, silently trusting its certificate would permit active interception. This spec therefore makes user-approved TOFU/pinning a required application-layer association and forbids the vendor client's disabled certificate and hostname checks.

unpair.clears: Only the client's stored certificate pin and selected machine, leaving machine Wi-Fi and saved data intact.

procedures.basis: Replacement-client trust policy derived from the requirement to correct the vendor client's trust-all TLS behavior; no machine state is changed.
procedures.name: Remove the client-side machine certificate pin

steps.action: Delete the selected machine and its stored certificate or SHA-256 pin in the client.
Repeat the explicit fingerprint-approval step before any later /info request.

issued_to_client: User-approved machine certificate or its SHA-256 pin
credentials.notes: The Wi-Fi key is typed directly into the machine, so no provisioning transport encryption is claimed. The monitoring API has no account token. The client-side certificate pin is a trust decision, not a device-issued credential and must not be shared across machines.
stored_on_device: Wi-Fi SSID and network key entered through the machine UI

factory_reset.description: Reset is a physical, on-machine procedure, never an API call. The full deletion procedure below is specific to PR1060W's addendum. EV1/EV1LE documents a network reset, and PR1055X/PR1060W documents Reset network operations. Other variants must use their own current manuals; the absence of a universal procedure is intentional.
factory_reset.effect: PR1060W Reset to Default deletes all saved data, customized settings and network information. EV1/EV1LE also exposes a network-settings reset. Do not generalize the scope or screen labels to every variant.

procedures.basis: Brother PR1060W Addendum to Operation Manual, Before Lending or Disposing of the Product (Resetting the Machine), page 13; not run by this project.
procedures.indicator: The manual warns not to turn off the machine during the reset; it gives no separate LED completion pattern.
procedures.name: PR1060W: full Reset to Default

steps.action: Open Settings and then the general settings screen.
Locate Reset to Default in the Settings pages and touch Reset.
steps.expect: Saved data, customized settings and network information are deleted.

steps.action: Leave the machine powered until the on-screen process finishes.
steps.notes: The addendum explicitly says not to turn off the machine during the process.

procedures.basis: Brother EV1/EV1LE Operation Manual, Wireless LAN Settings, page 26; not run by this project.
procedures.indicator: No separate completion indicator is documented; reconfigure the SSID afterward.
procedures.name: EV1/EV1LE: reset network settings

steps.action: Open Settings, then Wireless LAN Settings on page 11.
Choose Reset network settings and follow the on-screen instructions.
steps.expect: Network information is cleared so the machine can join a new network. This entry is not claimed to erase all saved designs.

procedures.basis: Brother PR1055X/PR1060W Operation Manual, Wireless LAN settings, page 27; not run by this project.
procedures.indicator: No separate completion indicator is documented; the connected SSID must be configured again.
procedures.name: PR1055X/PR1060W: reset network operations

steps.action: Open Settings and select Wireless LAN settings.
Choose Reset network operations and follow the on-screen instructions.
steps.expect: Network operations are reset. This narrower procedure is not the PR1060W full-data Reset to Default above.

methods.description: Join the machine to the owner's 2.4 GHz wireless network with its own touchscreen. The PR1055X/PR1060W manual excludes WPA/WPA2 Enterprise; check the exact model's manual before assuming another authentication mode. After the machine reports Connected, run safe SNMP discovery and explicit certificate approval. No design transfer is part of setup.
methods.name: On-machine wireless LAN setup

steps.action: Confirm the exact model is listed in this spec and, for XP1/XJ1/XE1/BP3600, install and activate Upgrade Kit I before attempting monitoring.
steps.expect: The machine has the documented My Stitch Monitor entitlement; an unupgraded base model is not assumed compatible.

steps.action: Open the machine's wireless LAN settings, enable wireless LAN, and start its connection wizard or Wireless LAN Connection screen.
steps.notes: EV1/EV1LE uses the Wireless LAN Connection flow on manual page 32; PR1055X/PR1060W uses the setup wizard on pages 29–31. Other models use the equivalent screen in their own manual.

steps.action: Select the home SSID, or Add network for a hidden SSID, then enter the network key on the machine and connect.
steps.expect: The machine displays Connected beneath the SSID. PR1055X/PR1060W requires 2.4 GHz 802.11b/g/n and does not support WPA/WPA2 Enterprise.

steps.action: Keep Wireless LAN Enable on, then discover the machine with the SNMP rules in this spec.
steps.expect: A response with matching request ID and exact host-resources description brother sewing.

steps.action: Show the discovered address and TLS certificate fingerprint; approve it only for an in-memory pin bound to that address and any discovered MAC, then fetch /info.
steps.expect: The client holds the approved pin only in memory and has not created a persistent machine-id binding.

steps.action: Require a nonempty machine-id, expected /info field types, and monitoring.version or monitoringpr.version above zero, or monitoring.availableversion whose first dotted component is 1; then atomically persist the pin to machine-id before any other endpoint.
steps.expect: /info validates identity and capability before the durable trust binding exists. A zero or missing capability is not support.

troubleshooting.fix: Keep Wireless LAN Enable on and select the saved SSID again, or repeat the on-machine connection flow with the current key. A full machine reset is not the first recovery step.
troubleshooting.symptom: The machine previously joined the network but does not reconnect.

setup.notes: Wireless provisioning is performed on the machine, not with an Artspira account. EV1's manual uses Wireless LAN Connection; PR1055X/PR1060W uses the Wireless LAN Setup Wizard. The other models have model-specific screens and upgrade requirements, so do not force one model's labels onto the family. The local read-only API needs no cloud account.

rejoin.notes: A router or SSID change is handled on the machine. EV1 offers saved networks; PR1055X/PR1060W can select a saved SSID in its wireless settings. The old network does not need to remain available. Use a network reset only when ordinary reconnection fails, and reserve the PR1060W full-data reset for transfer/disposal.

steps.action: Open the machine's wireless LAN settings with the new router running.
Select the new SSID and enter its key, or choose a previously saved SSID and connect.
steps.expect: The machine displays Connected; no factory reset or cloud account is needed.

steps.action: Rediscover the address and require the existing certificate pin, or ask the user to approve a changed certificate rather than silently accepting it.

testing.notes: No compatible machine was contacted and no machine packet capture was reviewed. Protocol facts are reported from the public Android monitor app, the public Design Database Transfer desktop client, official model lists and manuals. The 84-byte SNMP request is desktop-derived, not a capture. JSON examples are synthetic and independently parsed by scripts/test_brother_embroidery_lan.py.

evidence.app_static_analysis: The current and earliest public My Stitch Monitor Android implementations supplied the ordered directed/limited broadcast discovery, exact host description, OID roles, four read-only paths, capability versions, JSON property names/types, time units and status mapping. Their write-capable shared methods were reviewed only to exclude them. No vendor internal symbols are reproduced here.

evidence.desktop_static_analysis: Design Database Transfer 1.2.0 independently supplied an 84-byte SNMPv1 request containing host description, physical address and Brother IP-data varbinds. It is a static executable-data derivation, not a capture and not evidence that design transfer is safe or understood.
evidence.documentation_review: Brother's official app compatibility page, PR1060W product page and model manuals supplied variant coverage, upgrade-kit requirements, wireless provisioning, saved-network rejoin and model-specific reset procedures. All linked manuals were checked as resolving on 2026-11-17.
evidence.open_questions: No hardware evidence establishes actual certificate contents, complete response documents, coordinate/storage units, field-presence variation, concurrent-client behavior or per-model reset consistency. Unknown JSON fields and unknown status codes must remain forward-tolerant.
evidence.tls_defect_analysis: The vendor client's certificate-chain and hostname checks were found to be permissive. The spec deliberately replaces them with explicit user-approved TOFU/pinning and never treats that vendor defect as a compatibility need.

excluded_operations.rule: Do not turn shared-library method names into endpoints. Only the four entries in http_endpoints are allowed.

capability_gate.absent_or_zero: Do not enable monitoring; absence is not converted into proof of support.
capability_gate.model_id_rule: Never require or infer an EV1-specific numeric model ID.

json_parser.content: Parse one JSON object, reject trailing non-whitespace data and truncated JSON.
json_parser.known_property_types: Require the declared JSON types when a known property is present. A wrong type is an error, not a coerced zero/false.
json_parser.missing_properties: Leave unavailable rather than defaulting to a real measurement. Capability fields are the exception only in that missing means unsupported.
json_parser.numeric_ranges: RGB components accept 0..255; negative colorchange means not a change; ids and counters are not silently clamped.
json_parser.unknown_properties: Ignore unknown properties at every object/array element; they never change known-field meanings. Preserve the raw document for forward diagnostics when practical.
json_parser.unknown_status_values: Render unknown(<numeric value>) without assigning a known state, ready label or error class.

https_monitoring.timeout_basis: Reported monitor-app read timeout, not a hardware limit.

bootstrap.machine_id_validation: A nonempty string is required; its internal format and mapping to numeric model/type are not assumed.
ordered_steps: Show the discovered address and certificate fingerprint and require user approval before the first GET.
Hold the approved certificate or pin only in memory against the discovered address and MAC when available; do not persist it yet.
Fetch /info with the volatile pin and require a nonempty machine-id, expected JSON field types and monitoring capability; confirm the discovered address has not changed.
Atomically persist the certificate or pin to the validated machine-id, retaining address/MAC as metadata, before any /status, /embinfo or /embstatus request.

tofu.changed_certificate: Stop and ask the user again; never automatically accept a replacement. Repeat the volatile /info validation before replacing the durable binding.
tofu.fingerprint: SHA-256 of the presented DER certificate, lowercase colon-separated hex
forbidden: durable pin-to-machine-id before the first /info response
tofu.persist: After validated /info, atomically bind the approved certificate or fingerprint to machine-id, not to a model family. A durable binding must not be created before /info.
tofu.vendor_defect_not_reproduced: The reviewed vendor client disables both certificate-chain and hostname verification. This is a defect to correct, not interoperability evidence.

entries.evidence: Official app list (spelled EV1-LE) and shared operation manual.
Official app list; sewing-only CX1 is not claimed.
Official app list; Upgrade Kit I is required.

Official product page explicitly names My Stitch Monitor, although the global app list omitted this model when checked; treat that discrepancy as unresolved rather than dropping the model or claiming the whole PR family.

exclusions: PP1/PP1E use a separate BLE protocol and are not monitoring variants.
Artspira or Design Database Transfer support alone does not prove My Stitch Monitor support; NQ/NS/PE/SE/LB Wi-Fi models are therefore not added.
CX1, Dream Machine, Quattro, Essence, PR1050X and other models absent from the monitor evidence are not claimed.
model_compatibility.rule: The variant list records documented My Stitch Monitor compatibility, not a model-ID discovery matcher. Actual monitoring still requires exact SNMP identity plus /info capability and a user-approved certificate.

desktop_derived_request.encoding: BER: outer SEQUENCE, version 0, OCTET STRING public, GetRequest 0xa0, request ID, error status/index zero, three varbinds with NULL values and long-form lengths.
desktop_derived_request.provenance: Design Database Transfer 1.2.0 static data; DESKTOP-DERIVED, NOT A NETWORK CAPTURE

ordered_targets.target: Each active IPv4 interface's directed subnet broadcast

ordered_targets.only_if: No valid machine was found by the directed attempt; make this one limited fallback, not an unbounded address sweep.

request_id.rule: Generate a cryptographically fresh integer in 1..2147483647 for every newly encoded datagram, including the limited-broadcast fallback. Reuse an ID only for an identical retransmission. Match the response ID before accepting any values.

snmp_discovery.timeout_basis: Reported monitor-app socket timeout, not a hardware requirement.

status_codes.default: waiting in the vendor app; a safe replacement MUST instead return unknown(<value>) because an unlisted value has no established meaning
status_codes.source: Monitor app's current status-to-display mapping, reported rather than hardware-confirmed.

remaining_unknowns: No live SNMP response, TLS certificate or JSON document has been captured; every endpoint and field remains reported and interoperability is unverified.
Physical units for feature/hoop/design/x/y coordinates, previewresolution, hoopresolution, postsize and storage capacity/free are unestablished.
Semantics of emb, linkstatus, hoop.type, numeric model/type and most OEM values are unestablished.
Compatibility-list discrepancy for PR1060W needs a live check; BP regional aliases and exact upgrade/firmware states need per-unit confirmation.
Reset-to-default and network-reset screens are not established for every listed variant; use the exact model manual instead of generalizing the procedures here.
Concurrent-client limits, certificate rotation behavior, error responses and whether every listed firmware exposes identical JSON field presence are unknown.
Write, design-transfer, image, push, lens and firmware protocols are intentionally not reverse engineered or declared by this spec.
